extracted.intended_audience: school and college administrators, Title IX coordinators, investigators, decisionmakers, and legal counsel for recipients of federal education funding
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory preamble explaining required standards and procedural safeguards for recipients' Title IX grievance procedures, including who may file, when a Title IX Coordinator may initiate a complaint, equitable-treatment rules, conflict-of-interest and anti-bias requirements, investigative and appeal requirements, and supportive measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title IX Coordinator authority to initiate complaints
rubrics_metrics.description: The Title IX Coordinator may initiate a complaint only in the absence of a complaint (or after withdrawal/termination of informal resolution) and only after determining that the alleged conduct “presents an imminent and serious threat to the health or safety of a complainant or other person, or that conduct as alleged prevents the recipient from ensuring equal access based on sex to its education program or activity.” (§106.44(f)(1)(v))
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The final regulation was revised to make explicit that initiation by a Title IX Coordinator is limited and fact-specific; initiation requires the determination specified in §106.44(f)(1)(v). The Title IX Coordinator does not become the complainant by initiating a complaint and should not be read to “stand in” for the complainant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factors Title IX Coordinator must consider before initiating a complaint
rubrics_metrics.description: In making the determination to initiate a complaint under §106.44(f)(1)(v), the Title IX Coordinator must consider, at a minimum, the factors listed in §106.44(f)(1)(v)(A)(1)-(8).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Those factors include: (1) the complainant's request not to proceed; (2) the complainant's reasonable safety concerns about initiation; (3) the risk that additional acts of sex discrimination would occur if procedures are not initiated; (4) the severity of the alleged sex discrimination (including conduct that might require removal of a respondent to end discrimination); (5) the age and relationship of the parties, including whether the respondent is an employee; (6) the scope of the alleged discrimination (pattern, ongoing, multiple individuals impacted); (7) the availability of evidence to assist a decisionmaker; and (8) whether the recipient could end the alleged sex discrimination and prevent recurrence without initiating grievance procedures. These factors help balance the complainant's wishes with safety and effectiveness considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may file a complaint (scope of complainant standing)
rubrics_metrics.description: A complaint alleging sex-based harassment may only be made by a complainant (the person alleged to have been subjected to the discrimination), a parent/guardian/authorized legal representative, or the Title IX Coordinator; complaints of sex discrimination other than sex-based harassment may be made by those persons and additionally by any student or employee, or any person who is participating or attempting to participate in the recipient's education program or activity at the time of the alleged discrimination. (§106.45(a)(2))
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department emphasizes complainants must have some relationship with the recipient; allowing some non-aggrieved persons to file for non-harassment sex discrimination is intended to effectuate Title IX's broad statutory protection and is not unlimited. Recipients retain dismissal options under §106.45(d) (permissive dismissal) when the alleged conduct, even if true, would not constitute sex discrimination under Title IX.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complaint as a request to initiate grievance procedures; Title IX Coordinator not the complainant
rubrics_metrics.description: A complaint is essentially a request to initiate the recipient's grievance procedures and prompts investigation and determination whether sex discrimination occurred. A complaint initiated by a Title IX Coordinator under §106.45(a)(2) is not a complaint made on behalf of the Title IX Coordinator and the Coordinator does not become a party by initiating it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When the Title IX Coordinator initiates a complaint under the limited circumstances in §106.44(f)(1)(v), the complaint is based on the Coordinator's determination about threat to health/safety or impediment to equal access; references to “the parties” should not be read to refer to the Title IX Coordinator as the complainant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treat complainants and respondents equitably throughout the grievance procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients' grievance procedures must treat complainants and respondents equitably throughout the process. (§106.45(b)(1))
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Equitable treatment is not limited to offering supportive measures or following grievance procedures before imposing sanctions; recipients must ensure fairness and the ability of both parties to engage fully in procedures. The requirement applies regardless of the sex of the parties and complements nondiscrimination obligations in §106.31.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equitable (not strictly equal) treatment explained and bounded
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department retains the term “equitably” rather than “equally,” recognizing that fairness may require different treatment of parties depending on circumstances. (§106.45(b)(1))
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department declined to preserve the 2020 amendments' two illustrative examples as exclusive; instead, equitable treatment is implemented through other regulatory requirements (e.g., impartial investigation, presumption of not responsible, objective evaluation of evidence). Equitable treatment acknowledges differing interests of complainant and respondent and allows different measures where appropriate (e.g., remedies for complainant if discrimination found; procedural protections for respondent).

rubrics_metrics.name: Trauma‑informed approaches permitted if compliant with regulations
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients may adopt trauma-informed or complainant-centered approaches in handling sex-based harassment or other sex discrimination cases so long as those approaches comply with the grievance procedure requirements, including fairness and impartiality. (§106.45 and §106.44)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department declined to mandate or prohibit particular terminology (e.g., “victim/survivor” vs. “complainant/accuser”). Trauma-informed practices must not create impermissible bias or violate other regulatory requirements; recipients retain discretion but must ensure compliance with impartiality and objective-evidence rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on conflicts of interest and bias for designated officials
rubrics_metrics.description: Title IX Coordinators, investigators, decisionmakers (and informal resolution facilitators) must not have conflicts of interest or bias for or against complainants or respondents generally, or an individual complainant or respondent. (§106.45(b)(2); §106.44(k)(4))
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This prohibition applies to all decisionmakers including those deciding appeals of dismissals; recipients must train personnel and may use training and procedural safeguards rather than categorical role exclusions. The Department declined to list specific job roles that presumptively constitute conflicts of interest, leaving recipients discretion to identify and avoid actual conflicts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objective evaluation of all relevant evidence; credibility determinations
rubrics_metrics.description: Grievance procedures must require an objective evaluation of all evidence that is relevant and not otherwise impermissible, and provide that credibility determinations must not be based on a person's status as a complainant, respondent, or witness. (§106.45(b)(6))
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This provision, together with training requirements, is intended to guard against stereotyping and biased credibility assessments (e.g., based on race, sex, sexual orientation, disability). Recipients must ensure investigators are trained to avoid prejudgment and to evaluate evidence objectively.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presumption that the respondent is not responsible until determination
rubrics_metrics.description: Grievance procedures must include a presumption that the respondent is not responsible for the alleged sex discrimination until a determination is made at the conclusion of the recipient's grievance procedures. (§106.45(b)(3))
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This presumption is a core procedural safeguard and interacts with requirements that grievance procedures be followed before imposing disciplinary sanctions on a respondent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasonable steps to protect privacy of parties and witnesses
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must take reasonable steps to protect the privacy of the parties and witnesses during the grievance procedures, subject to specified exceptions. (§106.45(b)(5))
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Privacy protections are balanced against investigatory and legal requirements; the regulation acknowledges limitations and exceptions but requires reasonable privacy protections where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supportive measures obligations — “as appropriate” and scope limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must offer supportive measures “as appropriate” to restore or preserve a party's access to the recipient's education program or activity, including measures designed to protect safety or the educational environment. (§106.2 definition of “supportive measures”; §106.44(g))
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a complainant is not a student or employee, the recipient's ability to provide supportive measures may be limited by lack of relationship; the regulation recognizes recipients need only offer supportive measures when appropriate and necessary to restore or preserve access.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissive dismissal authority for recipients
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients may dismiss a complaint on any of the bases listed in §106.45(d)(1)(i)-(iv), including if the recipient determines that the conduct alleged, even if proven, would not constitute sex discrimination under Title IX.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permissive dismissal helps prevent institutions from being compelled to process complaints that fall outside Title IX coverage; this applies regardless of who initiated the complaint (including non-aggrieved filers).

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeals and remedy for decisionmaker conflict/bias
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must offer an appeal at minimum the same as in comparable proceedings (§106.45(i)); for postsecondary institutions, §106.46(i) requires offering an appeal based on factors that would change material aspects of the matter, including procedural irregularity or decisionmaker conflict of interest or bias that would change the outcome.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department notes parties may file complaints with OCR if they believe the recipient has failed to comply with requirements related to appeals or conflicts of interest; recipients must ensure appeal procedures address bias/conflict concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training requirements addressing impartiality and bias
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigators, decisionmakers, Title IX Coordinators and others involved in grievance procedures must be trained to serve impartially, including how to avoid prejudgment of facts at issue, conflicts of interest, and bias. (§106.8(d))
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department rejects the view that the anti-bias provision is insufficient, noting training and multiple regulatory safeguards (equitable treatment, presumption of not responsible, objective evaluation, privacy protections, appeals) together protect process integrity. Smaller institutions may face challenges but are not exempt from the conflict/bias prohibition.
